PLAN THE WORK

Start with how you use the room.

A bath for a long soak, a shower for busy mornings, or a better use of a small space: the right starting point is what you need from the room. Think about storage, access and who uses the bathroom before choosing fittings.

The visible finish matters, and so does the plumbing behind it. Moving a basin, bath or toilet can affect water supplies, drainage and the scope of the work. Discuss those choices before ordering your suite.

GOOD TO KNOW

Your questions,
answered.

Can you help with a complete renovation?

Tell Connor what you want to change. Agree the scope, including any tiling, flooring, electrical work or other trades, in your written quote.

Can I keep the existing layout?

Keeping fittings in similar positions may reduce plumbing alterations. The existing pipework and condition of the room still need to be assessed.

Do you have photographs of your work?

Yes. The project gallery contains real supplied photographs of completed Grandison work.
